references.text: Earlier in the same passage, the oath and curse that the woman must take upon herself are described, as well as the effect of the water on her body if she is guilty.
Describes that the woman shall drink the bitter water that brings a curse, the same action performed in verse 27.
The theme of becoming a curse and a proverb among the peoples, corresponding to how the woman shall become 'a curse among her people'.
The prophet Jeremiah uses similar language about becoming a curse among all the nations of the earth.
Again, Jeremiah uses the expression of becoming a curse and a horror, which mirrors the language in Numbers 5:27.
God's judgment on the woman in Eden's garden includes pain connected to her womb, which can be seen in connection with the physical punishment described in Numbers 5:27.
Proverbs warns against adultery and its consequences, including disgrace and shame that are never wiped out.
